title: Charge transfer, optical line scanning and buried-channel CCDs
findings: The 1970 concept proposed imaging. The companion experiment measured charge transfer between adjacent MOS capacitors. The event already exists and now specifies the original result.

A July 1971 Popular Electronics account documents the operating 96-element Bell Labs scanner. Tompsett’s team published actual line-scan optical images in November, and RCA engineer A. Boornard independently describes the Bell imager and its earlier charge-coupling concept.

The May 1972 Fairchild prototype is documented in a contemporary report that the February 1973 test-bed report directly cites. A March 1973 commercial plan points back to the February account. The named CCD101 offer follows in May 1973.

A 1971 Bell Labs patent filing documents a buried-channel modification of the original CCD. The 1972 Walden paper verified the channel in a conductance test. Fairchild’s independent experiments document the imaging benefit in its own implementation.

Early and Smith independently document a human route from the early Bell CCD program to Fairchild. The evidence supports uptake of the broad principle and a separate architectural comparison for the buried channel.
frontier: Locate Fairchild laboratory-to-product drawings or change records for the 1972 array and CCD101, and compare with Kim and Dyck’s linear-array patent family CA1020656A. The design sequence is documented, while specimen identity, engineering revisions and the specific Bell buried-channel design transfer remain unresolved.

Check the original 1970 Applied Physics Letters 8-bit CCD shift register paper (DOI 10.1063/1.1653327) and Bell Labs lab notebooks for a separate early imaging demonstration. The 96-element record remains scoped to the device and images documented in 1971.

Check the original Bell silicon diode array camera-tube work and dated notebooks for the specific contribution to the CCD imaging idea. Inventors’ later accounts distinguish conceptual influence from the reason the CCD project began.

screen: Searched discovery, source and lead indexes for CCD, charge-coupled, line imager, buried channel, 96-element, 500-element and MOS capacitor. The extant Boyle–Smith concept already had the 1970 verification publication. The distinct Bell 96-element imager and Bell Labs buried-channel design lacked canonical records. The Fairchild record already represented the 1973 CCD101 offer.
limits: A CCD produces an analog readout of charge from spatial samples. No claim about digital recording, global priority, first sale, or the specific CCD in Kodak’s camera is proposed.
